```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
library(OECDscaleup)
dict <- variable_dictionary
na_blank <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x) | x == "", "", x)
supply_table <- function(ds) {
  d <- dict[dict$dataset == ds, ]
  coding <- ifelse(d$coding == "", d$format, paste0(d$format, "; ", d$coding))
  src <- ifelse(d$sbs_code == "", d$source, paste0(d$source, " (", d$sbs_code, ")"))
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    Variable = paste0("`", d$variable, "`"), Priority = d$priority, Definition = d$definition,
    `Format and coding` = coding, `Source (SBS code)` = na_blank(src), Notes = na_blank(d$notes),
    check.names = FALSE
  ))
}
use_table <- function(ds) {
  d <- dict[dict$dataset == ds, ]
  flags <- paste0(ifelse(d$money, "money variable", ""),
                  ifelse(d$money & d$negatives_missing, "; ", ""),
                  ifelse(d$negatives_missing, "negatives set to missing", ""))
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    Variable = paste0("`", d$variable, "`"), `The package needs it` = d$package_requirement,
    `What the package does with it` = d$package_use, Cleaning = flags, check.names = FALSE
  ))
}
```

OECD project on SME scaling up. For information: scaleup@oecd.org,
juergen.amann@oecd.org.

This article describes the firm-level input data of the scale-up pipeline
(`run_scaleup_pipeline()`): what
each variable should contain, how high a priority it has, and what the
package does with it. The trade package's extra input is described in
`vignette("input-trade-data")`. The same information is in the package
dataset `variable_dictionary` (`?variable_dictionary`), for use in code.

Before a run, `check_inputs(cfg)` checks the files in `input_dir` against
this dictionary: what would stop the build, what looks wrong or will be
lost, and what the build will do to the data. Its report holds counts,
shares and years only, never firm records, so it can be shared with the
OECD team.

## Files

The pipeline reads its inputs from `config$input_dir`, as `.dta`
files. `<CT>` is the two-letter country code given to `config_scaleup()`.

| File | Content | Needed |
|---|---|---|
| `base_financials_<CT>.dta` | Firm-level panel: one row per firm and year, basic variables with a standard naming structure and no derived indices (growth rates and the like) | always |
| `plants_RAW_<CT>.dta` | Establishment-level data: one row per plant and year | optional (gives `multiplant`) |
| `tl3_typology.dta` | OECD urban/rural typology of TL3 regions (package dataset `tl3_typology`) | when `base_financials` has `region_3d` |
| `exchange_rates.dta` | Eurostat annual average exchange rates (package dataset `exchange_rates`) | for the non-euro countries in `country_patches$non_euro` |

The two reference files ship with the package and can be written to the
input folder with, for example,
`haven::write_dta(tl3_typology, file.path(input_dir, "tl3_typology.dta"))`.

## General rules

1. **Missing values** are coded `.` in numeric variables and `"."` in
   string variables. The package also reads an empty string as missing.
2. **Money variables are in EUR thousand**, at current (nominal) prices.
   Values in national currency are converted to euros with the Eurostat
   annual average exchange rates
   ([ERT_BIL_EUR_A](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/ERT_BIL_EUR_A/default/table?lang=en)).
   A panel delivered in euros is declared with
   `config_scaleup(financials_unit = "EUR")`, and the build divides the
   money variables (column "Cleaning" below) by 1000. The build stops if the
   median turnover per employee of firms with 10 to 49 employees does not
   fit EUR thousand (above 5,000 or below 1).
3. **Sector codes** follow NACE Rev. 2 or NACE Rev. 2.1 (or ISIC Rev. 4),
   not ISIC Rev. 3 or NACE Rev. 1.1. The revision is declared with
   `config_scaleup(nace_revision = "2")` or `"2.1"`. A panel that switches
   from Rev. 2 to Rev. 2.1 gives the first Rev. 2.1 year as
   `nace_rev21_from`. The build checks the section letters against the
   divisions for the declared revision, stops on a mismatch, and converts
   Rev. 2.1 codes to Rev. 2, for which the sector rules are written.
4. **Regions** are NUTS codes of the 2021 classification.
5. **`year`** is the calendar year the data refer to, not the year the
   accounts were filed. A firm appears at most once per year.

## Priorities

* **Must-have**: the pipeline does not run without it, or its core indicators
  depend on it.
* **Nice-to-have, first order**: used for important breakdowns and
  indicators; please supply it if it is available.
* **Nice-to-have, second order**: supply it if it is easy to.

The priority is the OECD's request to the data providers. What the package
itself needs is in the second table of each section: some variables are
derived when absent (`age`, `exit`), and some are collected for future work
and not used yet.

## base_financials

### What to supply

```{r}
supply_table("base_financials")
```

### What the package does with it

```{r}
use_table("base_financials")
```

### Other columns the package reads

These are not part of the dictionary, but `base_financials` may carry them:

* `age_cat`: the age class instead of `birth_year`, coded 0 (0-5 years),
  6 (6-10 years) and 11 (11 years or more). With both supplied,
  `birth_year` is used for age and entry and the supplied `age_cat` is
  kept as the age class.
* `number_plants`, `multiplant`: if already present in `base_financials`
  (from an earlier run), they are kept for the firm-years without records
  in `plants_RAW`.
* `consolidation_code`: the type of accounts (codes as in Orbis). Where
  present, the scaler analysis (`run_scaler_analysis()`) gives a mid-cap
  status only to unconsolidated accounts (`U1`, `U2`).
* `country`: dropped.

## plants_RAW

The plant file is optional. Without it there is no `multiplant` indicator
and the tables have no breakdown by single- and multi-plant firms.

### What to supply

```{r}
supply_table("plants_RAW")
```

### What the package does with it

```{r}
use_table("plants_RAW")
```

## Sources and references

Sources: BR = business register; BD = business demography; SBS = structural
business statistics; ITGS = international trade in goods statistics; ITSS =
international trade in services statistics; IFATS = inward foreign
affiliates statistics.

* BACH Working Group (2015), *The Bank for the Accounts of Companies
  Harmonized (BACH) database*, ECB Statistics Paper No. 11:
  <https://www.ecb.europa.eu/pub/pdf/scpsps/ecbsp11.en.pdf>.
* ERICA Working Group (2018), *ERICA methodological note*:
  <https://www.eccbso.org/system/files/inline-files/Doc3.4_ERICAWG_ERICA%20methodological%20note_2018_F.pdf>.
* The SBS codes are from Eurostat (2021), *Methodological manual on European
  structural business statistics, 2021 edition*:
  <https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/3859598/13985433/KS-GQ-21-016-EN-N.pdf/e9410e2b-eba1-7a09-554b-dff3ac1df6bf?t=1639751446385>.
